title: The Owner Host and worker ship together. The supervisor mints a branded UUID `registrationToken` per logical add, invalidates it on removal, and replays it only for the same retained registration after process restart. Lifecycle, requests, ...

attrs.text: The Owner Host and worker ship together. The supervisor mints a branded UUID `registrationToken` per logical add, invalidates it on removal, and replays it only for the same retained registration after process restart. Lifecycle, requests, and cancellations echo that token with the share id; per-request `TunnelRequestToken` remains independent. IPC decoders refuse missing identities, and neither token enters Relay URLs or wire frames. Same-package IPC does not negotiate versions; Relay wire frames retain numeric ids and protocol version 1. Compatibility capabilities include `actor-credential` and `direct-connection`. An actor may also carry an optional `displayName` (presentation data only, used for attribution; authorization keeps using the identity triple), and an optional owner-verifiable `credential` (the protocol validates its type only; an owner verifies it before trusting the asserted identity, and absence keeps today's Relay-asserted semantics). A share spec may carry `connection`; absence reads as `{ mode: 'relay' }`, and a Relay that still owns the data path refuses a `direct` registration.

title: Owners declaring `share-access-state` receive committed, id-less ACL/mode/expiry snapshots with a durable monotonic version. The worker forwards snapshots only from its current socket; the Host clears authority on socket loss and refreshes ...

attrs.text: Owners declaring `share-access-state` receive committed, id-less ACL/mode/expiry snapshots with a durable monotonic version. The worker forwards snapshots only from its current socket; the Host clears authority on socket loss and refreshes the authenticated requests snapshot before external execution admission. An unavailable snapshot fails closed instead of borrowing persisted ACLs.

title: **Historical release support is not verified** — `tests/frames/v1` records concrete frames and refusal obligations, but does not identify a published Owner release. The gateway declares `LIVESHARE_PROTOCOL_VERSION` and implemented capabilit...

attrs.text: **Historical release support is not verified** — `tests/frames/v1` records concrete frames and refusal obligations, but does not identify a published Owner release. The gateway declares `LIVESHARE_PROTOCOL_VERSION` and implemented capabilities; the Relay rejects a declared mismatch and sends optional lifecycle frames only to declared consumers. These checks preserve recorded fields and explicit refusals, not a per-release translation or an unbounded support window.

title: `fileReferences/list` is classified `reader-session-read` and listed in the read role, but a share viewer cannot reach it: the method takes an `Agent` rather than a request naming a Session, so the Session resource resolver finds no Session...

attrs.text: `fileReferences/list` is classified `reader-session-read` and listed in the read role, but a share viewer cannot reach it: the method takes an `Agent` rather than a request naming a Session, so the Session resource resolver finds no Session to bind and the Gateway decides the call with no resource to check. The classification stays for when the method gains a request object; the `@` file picker therefore offers no files on the viewer page.

title: Registry file locking prevents concurrent file writes from dropping durable entries, but each registry reads its own in-memory snapshot. One running Host claims the owner state directory through `owner-host.json`, so a second Host on the sa...

attrs.text: Registry file locking prevents concurrent file writes from dropping durable entries, but each registry reads its own in-memory snapshot. One running Host claims the owner state directory through `owner-host.json`, so a second Host on the same home reads the shares without registering or changing them and refuses every `liveshareShares` operation that would change a record or contact the Liveshare server for one with `liveshareShares/owner-state-held`; adding Sources to a share in the dialog, the share list, and the audit read included. It still imports a credential, which is its own sign-in, but that import claims and re-registers nothing. A Host that a successor replaced detects it on its next share operation and refuses the same way. The claim is advisory, is reclaimed once its process is gone, and is still not a multi-host authorization service.

title: No runtime invariant companion is published: authorization is checked in the operations themselves, and this package has no separate invariant observer.

title: A worker restart re-registers retained shares but does not replay viewer streams; viewers recover through their transport. Registration refusals 401, 403, 410, and 426 stop that share’s reconnect loop until something registers it again: rep...

attrs.text: A worker restart re-registers retained shares but does not replay viewer streams; viewers recover through their transport. Registration refusals 401, 403, 410, and 426 stop that share’s reconnect loop until something registers it again: republishing or changing its tier does, and so does storing a credential for that Liveshare server, which registers the shares that address left offline. A restore presents the credential this host holds for the share’s Liveshare server whatever this host’s own expiry read says, because the Liveshare server renews the login behind it and only the Liveshare server decides whether that credential still authorizes; a new share is still refused on that same local read.

title: The access mode grants `view` admission, while effective fork/write authority comes from the share mode. Per-viewer execution levels and immediate cross-instance stop/cancellation completion are not established; cancellation cannot undo com...

attrs.text: The access mode grants `view` admission, while effective fork/write authority comes from the share mode. Per-viewer execution levels and immediate cross-instance stop/cancellation completion are not established; cancellation cannot undo committed writes. A grant that ends stops the running turn of each source Session only when a share viewer started it, so the owner's own turn keeps running; a turn this host cannot attribute is stopped with the grant. A write-to-readonly snapshot denies later writes but does not promise immediate cancellation of a running child turn.

title: Viewer file operations are confined by a path check against the granted root, so a local process that swaps a directory inside the grant for a symlink between the check and the open can redirect them; directory-handle anchoring is deferred ...

attrs.text: Viewer file operations are confined by a path check against the granted root, so a local process that swaps a directory inside the grant for a symlink between the check and the open can redirect them; directory-handle anchoring is deferred to a separate change. Viewer tools are limited to the confined read and search surface (`read`, `read_image`, `glob`, `grep`, `present`), the tools with no local file effect (`todo_write`, `skill`, `web_search`, `web_fetch`), the PTC transport `run_code`, and, at the write tier, bounded `edit` and `write`; `bash`, `pwsh`, `cua`, `plugin_manager`, the `schedule_*` tools, and no other name is granted. A `run_code` program is not bounded by the share: [Session tiers](#session-tiers) states what its program may reach.

attrs.text: The viewer does not reach the owner's workspace files or terminals: `workspaceFiles/*` and every `terminal/*` method stay owner-only at every tier, so the reader has no file preview and no shell. It also has no DSH core management authority; an installed plugin the owner opens can still change what that plugin owns.

title: Endpoint capabilities enumerate installed plugins' Remote methods from the live Typert registry in [`shareable-catalog.ts`](src/host/shareable-catalog.ts); DSH core service namespaces are excluded. There is no sandbox around a method call a...

attrs.text: Endpoint capabilities enumerate installed plugins' Remote methods from the live Typert registry in [`shareable-catalog.ts`](src/host/shareable-catalog.ts); DSH core service namespaces are excluded. There is no sandbox around a method call and no read/write classification: granting a method trusts that installed plugin's code, which runs in the Host process. A selected method is callable by every authenticated share viewer on the resources the policy binds, across the `global`, `session`, and `workspace` resource kinds.

title: The owner selects installed-plugin methods in the share panel through a global switch and per-plugin rows. The global switch is `none` (open nothing), `custom` (follow the per-plugin list), or `all` (open every method the live catalog offer...

attrs.text: The owner selects installed-plugin methods in the share panel through a global switch and per-plugin rows. The global switch is `none` (open nothing), `custom` (follow the per-plugin list), or `all` (open every method the live catalog offers). Each plugin is then off, all its methods, or a subset; a partial selection stores an explicit method list, so methods the catalog adds later stay closed until the owner saves again. Plugin rows use the package's localized title when one exists and otherwise fall back to the package segment or namespace; search and bounded scrolling keep a large catalog usable. The selection is share-wide: every admitted viewer may call a selected method on the resources the policy binds, and per-viewer method levels are not established. Method authorization is independent of the session tier; the core share roles still decide Session and Workspace calls. A selection naming a method the catalog no longer offers exposes nothing but stays stored until the owner saves again.

title: The `@` reference picker in the viewer's composer lists every Session on the owner Host, not only the shared Session and the reader's own forks: `sessionReferenceResolver/candidates` answers from the whole session index, so an admitted view...

attrs.text: The `@` reference picker in the viewer's composer lists every Session on the owner Host, not only the shared Session and the reader's own forks: `sessionReferenceResolver/candidates` answers from the whole session index, so an admitted viewer reads the id, title, and working-directory path of each Session there, and that directory path can name the owner's folders even though the reader can open none of those Sessions. The picker is a read surface only; a viewer who cites a Session it cannot open still gets that Session's snapshot prepared for its prompt. Shares whose titles or paths are themselves sensitive should not be admitted to viewers, or wait for a candidate list confined to visible Sessions.

title: **Filesystem watchers observe only the mounted VFS**: image seeding is silent and the VFS has no symlinks or external writers. `persistent`, `ref()`, and `unref()` preserve the Node API but cannot control a dedicated Worker's lifetime becau...

attrs.text: **Filesystem watchers observe only the mounted VFS**: image seeding is silent and the VFS has no symlinks or external writers. `persistent`, `ref()`, and `unref()` preserve the Node API but cannot control a dedicated Worker's lifetime because browsers expose no ref-counted event loop.

title: **Worker confinement is a VFS boundary, not kernel Landlock**: `read-only` and `workspace-write` run the unchanged `@deepseek-ai/node-addon-system/landlock-run` JavaScript and launcher argv, but the process layer implements the logical `lan...

attrs.text: **Worker confinement is a VFS boundary, not kernel Landlock**: `read-only` and `workspace-write` run the unchanged `@deepseek-ai/node-addon-system/landlock-run` JavaScript and launcher argv, but the process layer implements the logical `landlock-run` executable and enforces its grants on every shell filesystem request. `full` therefore covers the Worker command table and mounted VFS only; it does not claim arbitrary native-process execution or Linux kernel isolation.

title: **The worker bundle pins a path inside `@yarnpkg/parsers`** — the build resolves the package's own `lib/shell.js` instead of its root, whose barrel also re-exports the Syml parser and so drags js-yaml into a bundle that never parses that fo...

attrs.text: **The worker bundle pins a path inside `@yarnpkg/parsers`** — the build resolves the package's own `lib/shell.js` instead of its root, whose barrel also re-exports the Syml parser and so drags js-yaml into a bundle that never parses that format (around 175 kB, plus its module body at worker start). The path is derived from the package manifest, so a layout change fails the build rather than reinstating the barrel; upgrading the dependency means re-checking that the shell parser still lives there.

title: **The shell is not bash**: no loops, functions, `case`, job control, or process substitution — the grammar stops at pipelines, `&&`/`||`, subshells, groups, redirections, and expansion. `&` runs its command to completion in place, `sed` acc...

attrs.text: **The shell is not bash**: no loops, functions, `case`, job control, or process substitution — the grammar stops at pipelines, `&&`/`||`, subshells, groups, redirections, and expansion. `&` runs its command to completion in place, `sed` accepts only substitution scripts, patterns are JavaScript regular expressions, and the command table holds coreutils only (no `git`, no network tools).

title: **A shell process has no synchronous filesystem**: it reads and writes the host's VFS by message, because blocking on a reply would need `SharedArrayBuffer`, which requires a cross-origin isolation GitHub Pages cannot grant. Directory-walki...

attrs.text: **A shell process has no synchronous filesystem**: it reads and writes the host's VFS by message, because blocking on a reply would need `SharedArrayBuffer`, which requires a cross-origin isolation GitHub Pages cannot grant. Directory-walking commands therefore cost one round trip per entry, and two concurrent commands can interleave their writes.

title: **`node:dns/promises`, `node:vm`, `node:repl`, `node:net`, `node:sqlite`, `node:worker_threads` are structural stubs**: imports remain available for image packaging; every exposed call reports its refusal on the console and throws with Node...

attrs.text: **`node:dns/promises`, `node:vm`, `node:repl`, `node:net`, `node:sqlite`, `node:worker_threads` are structural stubs**: imports remain available for image packaging; every exposed call reports its refusal on the console and throws with Node's `ERR_FEATURE_UNAVAILABLE_ON_PLATFORM` code. Rows needing native DNS, a real process, a Node REPL, or realm isolation cannot run here.
